mainTopic: What is sold with a house, and whether attached things count as ground
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the משנה: if the seller says 'the house and everything in it,' everything is sold. The גמרא first asks whether the משנה can follow רבי מאיר, who says selling a vineyard includes its tools. The answer that only fixed tools are included is rejected, because the משנה lists the key right next to the door. So the גמרא concludes that the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר. Next, a ברייתא lists what comes with a house and what does not, and רבי אליעזר says anything attached to the ground counts as ground. A second ברייתא teaches that a pipe carved before being attached invalidates a מקוה, but one attached first and carved later does not. The גמרא asks whose view this is, since it seems to fit neither רבי אליעזר nor רבנן. It rules out the house case, which may only be about how generously a seller sells, and turns to רבי אליעזר's beehive ruling, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: All These Are Sold
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying that when the seller says 'the house and everything in it,' all the listed items are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה. If the seller sold 'the house and all that is in it,' then all the items listed earlier are included in the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה separated items that go with the house, like the door, from items that do not, like the key. This last line says those limits disappear when the seller uses broad language that covers everything inside.

phrases.english: All of them are sold.
phrases.notes: This applies when the seller said 'the house and everything in it.' Then even the key and other loose items go with it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the seller uses inclusive language, everything listed in the משנה is sold.

steps.title: Does the משנה Contradict רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר, who says selling a vineyard includes the vineyard's tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: Let us say our משנה is not like רבי מאיר. If it were like רבי מאיר, he says: one who sells a vineyard has sold the vineyard's tools.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. רבי מאיר says that when you sell a vineyard, its tools come with it, so by the same logic the key should come with the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the key is not sold with the house. רבי מאיר holds that a property's working tools go along with it. So it looks like the משנה cannot match רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (a suggestion the גמרא will test)
The tools and equipment used for a vineyard

phrases.english: Gemara:
Let us say our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Meir.
For if it were Rabbi Meir, doesn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַכֶּרֶם – מָכַר תַּשְׁמִישֵׁי כֶרֶם!
phrases.english: If he sold the vineyard, he sold the vineyard's tools!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests which תנא the משנה follows
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה could follow רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר includes a property's tools in its sale, but the משנה leaves the key out of a house sale.

steps.title: Fixed Tools Versus Unfixed Tools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה could follow רבי מאיר, because the vineyard tools are fixed there, while the house items here are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is רבי מאיר. There, the tools are fixed; here, they are not fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idea that the משנה could still be רבי מאיר. It splits the cases: the vineyard tools are fixed to the vineyard, but the key is not fixed to the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer limits רבי מאיר's rule to tools that are permanently set in place for that property. Under this reading, the key is left out simply because it is not fixed, so there is no argument.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces a defense)

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Meir:
There it is fixed; here it is not fixed.
phrases.notes: 'There' is רבי מאיר's vineyard; 'here' is the house items in our משנה, like the key.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by telling the two cases apart
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (fixed vs. not fixed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's rule seemed to cover all of a property's tools.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר's rule covers only fixed tools, and the key in the משנה is not fixed.

steps.title: The Key Is Listed Like the Door
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: the משנה pairs the key with the door, so the key must count as 'fixed' like the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches the key in the same way as the door. Just as the door is fixed, so too the key is fixed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from the previous step. The משנה mentions the key right alongside the door, so the key must be treated as 'fixed' too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה groups the key with the door, the key is a fixed item that belongs to the house. Yet the משנה still says it is not sold. So the 'not fixed' answer fails, and the contradiction with רבי מאיר returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the same way as

steps.confusionAlert: 'Fixed' here does not mean nailed down. A key is obviously loose, but because it belongs to a specific door, it counts as a fixed part of the house just like the door.

phrases.english: But it teaches the key in the same way as the door:

phrases.aramaic: מָה דֶּלֶת דִּקְבִיעָא, אַף מַפְתֵּחַ דִּקְבִיעַ!
phrases.english: Just as the door is fixed, so too the key is fixed!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'fixed vs. not fixed' answer entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording shows the key counts as fixed, like the door, yet it is still not sold.

steps.title: Conclusion: The משנה Is Not Like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes clearly that the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear: our משנה is not like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: With the defense gone, the גמרא accepts its first suggestion: the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה leaves out the key, even though it counts as fixed. רבי מאיר would include fixed tools, so the two cannot match. The משנה follows a view that is stricter about what comes with a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is clear (the גמרא's final answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about selling a house does not follow רבי מאיר, because it leaves out the key even though the key counts as fixed, like the door.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear:
Our Mishnah is not in line with Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the suggestion of step 2 after step 4 rejected the defense
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא Lists What Comes With a House
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what is sold with a house: the door, bolt, and lock, but not the key; a carved-in mortar but not an attached one; the lower millstone but not the upper one; and not the oven, stove, or hand mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: One who sells a house has sold the door, the bolt, and the lock, but not the key. He sold a mortar carved into the ground, but not one attached to it. He sold the lower millstone, but not the upper stone, and not the oven, the stove, or the hand mill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives its own list of what goes with a house sale and what stays with the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the same split as the משנה between door and key. It adds a finer point: a mortar carved out of the ground itself is part of the house, but a separate mortar attached later is not. Items like the oven, stove, and mill are not included.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who sells the house

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַדֶּלֶת וְאֶת הַנֶּגֶר וְאֶת הַמַּנְעוּל,
phrases.english: has sold the door, the bolt, and the lock,
but not the key.
He has sold the carved-out mortar,
phrases.notes: 'Carved' means hollowed right out of the ground, so it is really part of the house itself.

phrases.english: but not the attached one.
He has sold the lower millstone,
but not the upper stone,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַתַּנּוּר, וְלֹא אֶת הַכִּירַיִם,
phrases.english: not the oven, and not the double stove,
and not the hand mill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source on the same subject as the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house sale includes parts that belong to the building itself, like the door, bolt, lock, carved mortar, and lower millstone. It does not include the key, an attached mortar, the upper stone, the oven, the stove, or the hand mill.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Attached to the Ground Counts as Ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says anything attached to the ground is treated like the ground, so it is sold with the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Anything attached to the ground is like the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees with the first part of the ברייתא and gives a broad rule: whatever is attached to the ground counts as part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא left out an attached mortar. רבי אליעזר disagrees: once something is attached to the ground, it becomes part of the land. So it is included in the sale.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא separates items that are part of the house from items merely attached to it. רבי אליעזר says anything attached to the ground counts as ground and is sold.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Anything attached to the ground
is like the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever is attached to the ground is treated as ground and is included in the sale.

steps.title: Saying 'Everything Inside' Sells It All, But Never the Pit, Cistern or Gallery
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: if the seller says 'the house and everything in it,' all the items are sold. Either way, the pit, cistern and gallery are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller said, 'I am selling you the house and everything inside it,' then all those items are sold. But either way, he did not sell the pit, the cistern, or the gallery.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 6 ends by explaining what happens when the seller uses wider wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'everything inside it' also brings in the items that are normally left out, like the key and the upper millstone. But the pit, the cistern and the gallery are treated as separate things, not part of the house. So even the wide wording does not include them.

keyTerms.meaning: It and everything that is inside it: wide sale wording
A gallery or side structure attached to the house

steps.whatToRemember: Wide wording sells the movable house items too. The pit, cistern and gallery stay with the seller no matter what.

phrases.english: When he (the seller) said to him:
"It and everything that is inside it"
all of them are sold.
Either way,
phrases.notes: Whether he said just 'the house' or 'the house and everything in it.'

phrases.english: he did not sell the pit,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת, וְלֹא אֶת הַיָּצִיעַ.
phrases.english: nor the cistern, nor the gallery.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: הוּא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the house-sale ברייתא from Steps 6-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wide wording sells all the house items, but the pit, cistern and gallery are never included.

steps.title: A Carved Pipe and a Ritual Bath
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a pipe carved first and then fixed in place makes a מקוה invalid. A pipe fixed first and then carved does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: a pipe that someone carved out and then fixed in place makes a מקוה invalid. If he fixed it in place first and then carved it out, it does not make the מקוה invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about water flowing into a מקוה through a carved pipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A carved-out pipe that is free-standing counts as a כלי (vessel), and water that passes through a vessel spoils a מקוה. If it was carved while still loose, it became a vessel and stays one even after it is fixed in place. If it was fixed to the ground first, the carving happens to something attached to the ground, so it never becomes a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: A pipe or channel for water
He fixed it in place (attached it)

steps.confusionAlert: The order is what matters. Carving first and then attaching makes the מקוה invalid. Attaching first and then carving does not.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A pipe that one carved out and afterward fixed in place
invalidates the ritual bath.
If he fixed it in place and afterward carved it out,
it does not invalidate the ritual bath.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: צִינּוֹר שֶׁחֲקָקוֹ וּלְבַסּוֹף קְבָעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about attached objects, linked to רבי אליעזר's rule in Step 7 that attached things count as ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pipe carved before being fixed in place invalidates a מקוה. One fixed first and carved afterward does not.

steps.title: Whose View Is This? It Seems to Fit No One
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught this ברייתא, because it seems to fit neither רבי אליעזר nor רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is neither רבי אליעזר's nor רבנן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: the pipe ruling does not seem to match either side of a known argument. This sets up the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half (carved, then attached, still invalid) seems to go against רבי אליעזר, who treats attached things like the ground. The second half (attached, then carved, valid) seems to go against רבנן, who do not treat attached things like the ground. So the ברייתא appears to mix both views.

phrases.english: Whose view is it?
Neither רבי אליעזר nor the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? לָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who could have taught the ברייתא in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא about the pipe and the מקוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each half of the ruling seems to match only one side of the argument, so no single opinion fits the whole ruling.

steps.title: Which Ruling of רבי אליעזר Is Meant? Maybe the House
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ruling of רבי אליעזר it has in mind. It first suggests his ruling about selling a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי אליעזר do we mean? If you say it is רבי אליעזר's ruling about the house...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask exactly which argument between רבי אליעזר and רבנן it is talking about. It starts with the house-sale ruling from Step 7, and this sets up a rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To claim the ברייתא fits 'neither,' we must know which argument we are using. The first suggestion is the house case, where רבי אליעזר said anything attached to the ground is like the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: Which ruling of רבי אליעזר?
If you say רבי אליעזר's ruling about the house,
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from Step 7: anything attached to the ground is like the ground and is sold with the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּבַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies which argument the problem in Step 10 depends on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which argument between רבי אליעזר and רבנן the ברייתא is being compared to.

steps.title: The House Argument May Be About How Generous a Seller Is
steps.stepSummary: The house case cannot be the source. That argument may only be about whether a seller sells generously or sparingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is the reason there: רבי אליעזר holds that a seller sells generously, and רבנן hold that a seller sells sparingly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the house-sale ruling as the source for this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house case, רבי אליעזר and רבנן may not disagree about whether attached things are 'ground.' They may only disagree about how much a seller means to include in a sale. If so, that argument tells us nothing about a pipe and a מקוה.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is the reason:
that רבי אליעזר holds:
a seller sells with a generous eye,
and the Rabbis hold:
a seller sells with a stingy eye!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the house-sale argument as the source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That argument may be about how generously a seller sells, not about whether attached items count as ground.

steps.title: Then It Must Be רבי אליעזר's Beehive Ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns instead to רבי אליעזר's ruling that a beehive is like land, so a פרוזבול can be written based on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means רבי אליעזר's ruling about a beehive. As we learned in a משנה: about a beehive, רבי אליעזר says it is like land, and one may write a פרוזבול based on it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different ruling of רבי אליעזר as the source and starts quoting it. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אליעזר treats an attached beehive as true land, not just as part of a sale, since a פרוזבול can only be written if the borrower owns land. If this is the source, it would show that for him attached things really count as ground. The גמרא keeps testing this suggestion on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that stops שמיטה from canceling a loan; it needs the borrower to own land

phrases.english: Rather, רבי אליעזר's ruling about a beehive?
As we learned in a משנה: a beehive,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הִיא כַּקַּרְקַע –
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: it is like land,
and one may write a פרוזבול based on it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the house ruling is rejected in Step 12, the גמרא offers the beehive ruling instead.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposes that the argument meant is רבי אליעזר's beehive ruling, where an attached beehive is treated as real land. The suggestion is still being examined.
